PullRequest.Title: agentHost: make startup session discovery registry-first
PullRequest.Body:
agentHost: make startup session discovery registry-first (#331155)

A 2026-08-17 Insiders reproduction with 941 SDK sessions and 1,437
per-session databases (~946 MB) showed the ~60s delay is not migration —
`sessionRegistryBackfilled:copilotcli` was already true and migration was
skipped. The time went to per-session SQLite work during discovery and
listing: classification took 66.9s (113 external, 342 adoptable
extension-host, 486 already known), registration of the 113 emitted
candidates another 21.9s, and the first two AHP `listSessions` calls
109.8s and 91.0s, with a third 73.2s window after discovery.

Each measured phase is addressed:

- Classification (66.9s): discovery is now registry-first. `IAgent` gains
  an optional `setKnownSessionsFilter` seam that `AgentService` installs
  at provider registration; it answers, in one registry query for the
  whole candidate set, which sessions the host already owns.
  `CopilotAgent` drops those candidates instead of opening a session
  database each, so the 486 already-known sessions cost no DB opens.
  Tombstoned sessions are absent from the registry and therefore never
  reported as known, so an explicitly deleted session still reaches
  `register`, whose atomic tombstone check declines it. Provenance of a
  registered row stays owned by the explicit create/restore paths.

- Classification (the 342 adoptable rows): while migrate-legacy is off,
  adoptable extension-host candidates are never emitted, so their
  Git-touching project resolution is now skipped entirely instead of
  being computed and then filtered away. `_emitCopilotChats` keeps its
  filter as a re-check, since the setting can flip mid-pass.

- Registration (21.9s): `_registerDiscoveredChats` rejects an
  already-registered candidate with unchanged provenance before
  `_isChatBacking()` or any other per-session I/O.

- Listing (109.8s / 91.0s / 73.2s): `listSessions()` coalesces concurrent
  computations per external-sessions mode, so the burst a multi-window
  restore produces shares one registry traversal. The shared entry
  records the registry epoch it started at and every registry mutation
  invalidates it, so a caller arriving after a mutation starts a fresh
  pass rather than joining a possibly pre-mutation one. Each caller gets
  its own array; rejections are shared only with callers already waiting.

- `_readStoredSessionMetadata` / `_readSessionMetadata` now issue one
  bulk `getMetadataObject()` query instead of nine and six single-key
  reads, shrinking the cost of the fallback path that runs when no host
  filter is installed.

Deferred deliberately: seeding a newly discovered external session as
read still creates its database purely to hold one flag. Dropping the
write without a durable default would flip every discovered external
session to unread, because the list overlay only applies `IsRead` when
the key is present. The correct default belongs on the registry row and
is left to the registry list-projection change; the reasoning is
recorded on `_initializeExternalSessionReadState`. Removal of
`_awaitInitialProviderMigration()` is likewise not attempted: the
reproduction proves migration was already skipped.

Tests assert call/open counts rather than wall-clock thresholds:
registry-known candidates cause zero session DB opens; disabled
adoptable candidates resolve no projects; re-registering a known
discovered chat performs no per-session I/O; the known-sessions filter
reports registered sessions only and leaves tombstones to registration;
concurrent list calls share one computation but not their arrays; a
mutation during an in-flight list is not served from it; and stored
metadata is read with a single bulk query.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Startup discovery opened and queried one SQLite session database for every SDK catalog entry, including hundreds already represented in the host registry; work scaled with SDK session count despite the registry already containing the answer.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Large Copilot SDK catalogs caused tens of seconds of startup discovery latency from hundreds of unnecessary per-session SQLite opens and metadata reads.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Discovery now bulk-queries the authoritative registry once and drops registered candidates with in-memory Set membership before any per-session database I/O.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this PR, _discoverCopilotChats mapped every SDK session through _readStoredSessionMetadata; that helper calls tryOpenDatabase and issues metadata SQL for each session, under a limiter of four. The changed host filter performs one AgentSessionRegistry.list query for the full candidate set, and the changed Set lookup at line 2248 bypasses all per-session database opens for registered candidates. The added test instruments tryOpenDatabase and proves zero opens for registry-known candidates. The PR's reproduced 941-session startup attributes 66.9s to this classification path.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Discovery eagerly resolved projects through Git for adoptable sessions that the next stage always discarded; cost scaled with the number of distinct candidate working-directory/context keys, bounded only to four concurrent resolutions.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Startup discovery spent avoidable Git/project-resolution time on hundreds of legacy extension-host sessions while migration was disabled.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: When legacy migration is disabled, adoptable extension-host candidates are discarded immediately after marker classification, before project/Git resolution that cannot affect emitted output.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before the change, every unknown candidate reached _resolveSessionProject before _emitCopilotChats later filtered adoptable extension-host sessions when migration was disabled. _resolveSessionProject calls projectFromCopilotContext through a limiter and Git service; effective calls are deduplicated only by context key. The new guard at line 2257 runs after marker classification but before project resolution. The added test supplies an adoptable session with migration off and asserts getRepositoryRoot is never called.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A multi-window restore burst launched a complete registry traversal and per-session database-overlay pass for every concurrent IPC request, multiplying filesystem/SQLite work by the number of windows.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Concurrent startup list requests each took roughly 73-110 seconds and duplicated full-catalog SQLite work, increasing startup latency and I/O pressure.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Concurrent listSessions requests for the same external-session mode now share one registry traversal and one set of per-session metadata reads, while registry mutations invalidate sharing and each caller receives an independent array.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before the PR, each listSessions invocation independently awaited migration, traversed the registry, fetched provider metadata, and opened every listed session database for metadata overlay (with per-call limiters of four). The new per-mode in-flight map at line 1554 shares one _computeSessions promise; mutation epochs prevent post-mutation callers from joining stale work, and results are copied per caller. The added test proves two concurrent calls execute one computation. The reproduced multi-window startup recorded individual list calls of 109.8s, 91.0s, and 73.2s on a 1,437-database corpus.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot provider startup discovers SDK sessions and additively registers unknown sessions for surfacing.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For discovered sessions to appear, the provider must complete the SDK catalog RPC, the new registry filter, per-candidate classification, and AgentService registration. This work starts from the first discovery listener and is not awaited by provider registration, so it is off the host's basic startup critical path but is the critical path for session-list completeness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one RPC per discovery attempt, independent of S.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single SDK catalog RPC ran before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before classification and surfacing can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read all host registry session rows and intersect them with candidate URIs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SQLite SELECT over R rows per discovery pass, then O(S+R) in-memory Set work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider classification did not query the registry and instead attempted to open/query each candidate's session database; AgentService separately listed the registry only when candidates were emitted for registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before candidate classification, but replaces S per-session database probes for host-managed Copilot discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read vscode.metadata.json to classify extension-host sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold read per unknown session ID over the agent lifetime; later passes reuse cached promises.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same marker read occurred for every candidate that survived the old stored-metadata check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to distinguish adoptable candidates before filtering or project resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one resolution per distinct eligible context key P in a pass, with concurrency 4.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unknown adoptable sessions also performed this Git work even though _emitCopilotChats immediately filtered them when migration was disabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks metadata emission for eligible unknown sessions. The diff removes this boundary entirely for adoptable candidates when migration is disabled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register emitted sessions atomically and seed each new external session's read metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to E registry mutations and one per-session database write for each newly registered external session; concurrency is limited to 4.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same writes occurred for newly registered sessions, while repeated already-registered candidates additionally opened their databases for chat-backing checks before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before new sessions become registry-backed and are reconciled into the visible list.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: SDK catalog size S, registry size R, unknown candidates U, distinct project context keys P, and newly emitted sessions E. The reproduced large case has 941 SDK sessions; the new expensive classification work scales with U rather than all S for database access, Git work scales with eligible distinct P after per-pass coalescing, and registration scales with E.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One SDK catalog request and one registry query run serially before classification. Candidate classification is limited to 4; project resolution is separately limited to 4 and coalesced per context key within the pass. Registration is limited to 4. There is no unbounded subprocess, filesystem, or database burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Extension-host marker reads are promise-cached by session ID for the agent lifetime, including missing/malformed results. Project resolution is coalesced by context only within one discovery pass. The registry filter is recomputed per discovery pass so mutations are observed. With the host filter installed, known sessions do not open per-session databases; the optional fallback now uses one bulk metadata query per candidate.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call flow, limiter bounds, cache keys, database implementation, and added operation-count tests directly establish the boundary cardinalities.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact SDK RPC, Git, and SQLite duration varies by machine and catalog composition; an empty SDK catalog now performs a registry SELECT, but discovery is background and this bounded one-query edge case does not establish a user-visible regression against the removed per-candidate path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff replaces per-candidate SQLite fan-out with one registry query, prevents eager Git work for candidates guaranteed to be discarded, and short-circuits repeated registration I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: One or more restored windows request the Agent Host session catalog concurrently.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each client request waits for initial provider migration, registry enumeration, provider metadata lookup, per-session metadata overlay, filtering, and IPC response serialization. Concurrent requests for the same mode and registry epoch now wait on one shared computation; response array copying and serialization remain per caller.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request and one serialized response per window refresh; W requests remain, but host-side computation is coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each request independently triggered the complete host computation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each window waits for the shared host computation and its own response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registry SELECT per active mode/epoch computation rather than one per concurrent caller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every listSessions call issued its own registry traversal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks all metadata processing for the shared computation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch provider metadata for each registered session, including Copilot getSessionMetadata RPC
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one provider metadata lookup per registered session N in a computation, limited to 4; coalescing removes duplicate sets across same-mode concurrent callers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each concurrent list call repeated these per-session provider lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks inclusion of each registry row in the shared result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open each returned session database and bulk-read list overlay metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one open and one bulk metadata query per listed session N in a computation, limited to 4.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every concurrent call repeated this full per-session database overlay pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks completion of the catalog result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy the result array and serialize it for each IPC caller
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One O(N) shallow array copy per caller plus the pre-existing response serialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each caller already owned a separately computed array and serialized its own response, so there was no extra shallow copy but all O(N) metadata and database work was duplicated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded per-caller CPU/allocation after shared computation, while avoiding substantially larger duplicated metadata objects and boundary work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Registered session count N, concurrent callers W, and external-session modes M. Before the PR the dominant boundary work scaled as O(W*N); after the PR it scales as O(K*N), where K is the number of distinct active mode/epoch computations and K is no greater than W.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one computation per external-session mode and registry epoch is shared. Registry mutations clear sharing so a post-mutation caller starts a new computation. Within a computation, provider metadata and session overlay work are each limited to 4; no global unbounded concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: This is in-flight coalescing only, not a settled-result cache. Entries are removed on fulfillment or rejection and invalidated on registry mutation. Rejections are shared only by current waiters. Each caller receives a distinct shallow-copied array, so mutable result ownership is not shared.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: map keying, epoch invalidation, cleanup, limiters, and the added test proving one computation for two concurrent calls are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The savings depend on overlap, mode equality, N, and provider/database latency. The shallow-copy cost is not benchmarked, but its N reference assignments are dominated by the eliminated full metadata computations and cannot increase the number of computations over pre-change behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Coalescing bounds duplicated registry/provider/database work while preserving mutation freshness and caller-owned arrays.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot session metadata is read during resume, listing fallback, discovery fallback, and session operations.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For call sites that need persisted metadata, opening the session database and reading all requested keys must finish before metadata parsing and the operation can proceed. Fire-and-forget project persistence is off the caller's critical path, but the changed read helpers themselves remain synchronous dependencies of their callers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read six persisted Copilot session metadata keys
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One database open and one IN query per invocation instead of six single-key SQL queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same keys were fetched through six concurrent getMetadata calls, resulting in six SQLite statements on one database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks consumers such as customization-anchor and resume/config resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read nine persisted Copilot discovery/project metadata keys
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One database open and one IN query per invocation instead of nine single-key SQL queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same keys were fetched through nine getMetadata calls, resulting in nine SQLite statements on one database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks provider metadata and fallback discovery classification when this helper is used.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of metadata helper invocations Q and keys K (6 for _readSessionMetadata, 9 for _readStoredSessionMetadata). Database opens remain Q, while SQL statements fall from Q*K to Q.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The helper issues one SQLite query per invocation. Outer callers retain their existing bounds, including discovery's limiter of 4; the diff does not introduce a new concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new long-lived cache is added. Each call reads current database values through the existing session database reference. Missing keys are returned explicitly as undefined by the bulk query.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: SessionDatabase.getMetadataObject builds one parameterized IN query, and the added test records exactly one bulk call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Per-query latency varies and the registry-first discovery path now bypasses this helper for known sessions, but statement-count reduction is directly established and no larger payload is selected than the same fixed key set.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The fixed-size bulk query strictly reduces SQLite statement fan-out without changing lifetime or concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review over the full six-file diff. No actionable performance regression was introduced. Recorded three concrete shipped-regression fixes: registry-first discovery removes per-session SQLite fan-out, disabled migration skips eager Git project resolution, and same-mode listSessions calls coalesce full catalog computations.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
